title: Case: Sewing machine ten days late, one delivery attempt, recipient still without it
context: Greer Jessop ordered a sewing machine from Tallowmere Goods (TG-5325 / DL-7596), due 21 February. She has phoned the Saltmarrow Arc support line twice.
initial_request:
Let me set this out so nobody can say it wasn't clear.
1. Due 21 February. Arrived at my street 3 March. TEN days late.
2. ONE attempt. I was in. Nobody knocked.
3. Your driver PHOTOGRAPHED MY FRONT DOOR. I have seen the photo in the tracking. So he was there with the parcel.
4. The next day it is 'lost in network'. Lost where? Between my doorstep and his van?
5. 5 March: promised an email in 24 hours. NOTHING.
6. 7 March: promised an email by end of next day. NOTHING.
Do not tell me someone will be in touch. I have been told that twice. I want to know where my sewing machine is.

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the contradiction to them: a driver photo at the door of 6 Sallow Row at 16:12 on 3 March with no handover, against a 'lost in network' status set on 4 March; ask them to review the stop and say what happened to the parcel.

must: Sends the contradiction to Delivery investigations: driver photo at the front door at 16:12 on 3 March with no handover recorded, against the 'lost in network' status set by the depot audit on 4 March
Asks them to review the stop record and photo and establish what happened to the parcel after the stop, without stating which record is right

Tells the team that she waited ten days for one attempt and was twice promised a follow-up email by the support line (5 and 7 March) that never came, so they can prioritise and so the next update she gets is a real one
must_not: Promises Greer Jessop another follow-up, update or email by a stated time
States that the parcel is lost, or that it was delivered or left at her door
Promises or implies a refund or replacement
Suggests theft, or that she or the driver is at fault, on the strength of the photo
Sends her a generic apology for the delay that does not engage with the two missed follow-ups
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the claim from Quillon Pendlebury (who has no recorded link to DL-7596) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Quillon Pendlebury's message
expected.reference_message: Please review the 3 March stop for DL-7596 / TG-5325 (Greer Jessop, 6 Sallow Row, sewing machine). Two records conflict. Dispatch shows a stop at 16:12 on 3 March with a driver photo of the front door, number 6 visible, status 'attempted', and no handover, signature, safe-place note or card logged. Parcel trace then set the parcel to 'lost in network' at 23:50 on 4 March because it was not on the returns shelf or the van manifest; they have not looked at the stop or photo and say those sit with you. The recipient says she was in and nobody knocked. Please establish what happened to the parcel between the photo and the end of that route, and tell me what you find and when. I am not assuming loss or delivery. For priority: the parcel was already ten days late, this was the only attempt, and the support line promised her an email on 5 March and again on 7 March; neither was sent. I have not promised her anything further and would rather give her a finding than a third promise.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3202: people, organisations and references renamed. 35 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. An unverified bystander, Quillon Pendlebury, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
